description:
Let’s face it: space learning is usually trapped inside flat, dusty textbooks. We figured the cosmos deserved a massive upgrade!

Powered by code, late-night brainstorming, and a passion for storytelling, team The Orbitauts is stepping in to turn ordinary screens into infinite cosmic windows. We're on a mission to transform space science into an actual adventure!
summary:
Orbitarium is a free, browser-based space mission simulator where players learn aerospace engineering by flying it. Orbital mechanics is usually locked behind telemetry tables and heavy math, while most educational space tools stop at passive quizzes. Orbitarium replaces both with a continuous 60 fps simulation organized around the four segments of a NASA-style mission architecture: Launch, Space, Ground, and User.

Players fly handcrafted missions: tracking hurricanes from orbit, rescuing Lunar Gateway cargo with a Canadarm-inspired grapple, and mapping Martian polar ice. Along the way they steer ascent trajectories, execute orbital burns, deflect solar flares, and downlink telemetry during ground-station line-of-sight windows. Trajectory physics is fixed-timestep two-body motion with live trajectory prediction arcs, informed by NASA’s GMAT.

Orbitarium makes systems-engineering trade-offs and international collaboration intuitive for learners aged 12+, with no installation and no astrodynamics background.
details:
The Vitalauts' Project Solution

Orbitarium is a free, browser-based space mission simulator where players learn aerospace engineering by flying it. Orbital mechanics is traditionally locked behind dense telemetry tables and heavy math, while most educational space tools stop at passive quizzes. Orbitarium replaces both with a continuous 60 fps simulation organized around the four core segments of a NASA-style mission architecture: Launch, Space, Ground, and User. By combining interactive spacecraft assembly with live physics, our platform makes systems-engineering trade-offs and orbital maneuvers intuitive for learners of all backgrounds.

How Does Our Solution Work

Imagine trying to master rocket science through static textbook equations and dry velocity tables—it's overwhelming and disconnected from how space missions actually work. Instead, you open Orbitarium and take direct command.

Orbitarium guides players through a smooth, hands-on mission lifecycle:

  • 3D Systems Designer & Component Bay: Players enter a sleek assembly hangar to configure their spacecraft structure, propulsion, power, and scientific payloads. Every design choice impacts mass, fuel consumption, and operational limits.

    Launch & Ascent Flight Corridor: Players manually steer their ascent trajectory, timing throttle burns and banking through booster rings to clear the atmosphere while conserving vital propellant for orbit insertion.
    Orbital Operations & Hazard Avoidance: Powered by live trajectory prediction arcs, players execute orbital burns around Earth, the Moon, or Mars. Along the way, they fly handcrafted missions—tracking hurricanes from orbit, rescuing Lunar Gateway cargo with a Canadarm-inspired robotic grapple, and dodging unpredictable solar flares or space debris.
    How Is Our Project Creative & What Factors Did Our Team Consider?

Most educational software feels like an intimidating, dry simulator or a passive click-through presentation. We took a creative, human-centered approach by designing Orbitarium like an engaging, visual sci-fi mission control dashboard where real astrodynamics feel natural and fun.

While building Orbitarium, our team (The Vitalauts) carefully weighed several real-world aerospace factors:

  • Zero Barrier to Entry: Designed to run 100% locally in any browser with zero installation, zero downloads, and no prior astrodynamics background required.
  • Interconnected Systems Thinking: Every phase directly affects the next—wasting fuel during launch makes orbital maneuvering harder, and missing ground-station passes delays data delivery.
  • Visual Clarity Under Pressure: Complex orbital mechanics are communicated through intuitive visual cues (apoapsis/periapsis markers, warning trajectories, and signal cones) rather than raw text tables.
  • Cross-Platform Accessibility: Built with responsive scaling so it runs smoothly across different devices and screen sizes.
    The System Benefits
    Orbitarium benefits students, educators, and space enthusiasts by:
  • Bridging Theory and Practice: Replaces passive quizzes with active piloting, letting players physically experience how gravity, momentum, and thrust interact.
  • Making Systems Engineering Intuitive: Teaches real trade-offs between spacecraft mass, power limits, and fuel consumption through gameplay.
  • Engaging the Next Generation: Sparks genuine curiosity for aerospace careers by making complex NASA frameworks accessible to learners aged 12 and up.

    Our Goal & Intended Impact
    Our goal is to make aerospace engineering and orbital mechanics approachable, intuitive, and exciting for everyone. By letting students directly experience how launch decisions, orbital adjustments, and ground-station windows depend on one another, Orbitarium's intended impact reaches far:
  • In Classrooms & Homes: Empowers students and teachers with a free, immersive tool to explore space science without expensive equipment or heavy math prerequisites.
  • Inspiring Future Explorers: Builds foundational intuition for orbital mechanics that inspires tomorrow's aerospace engineers, mission controllers, and space scientists.

    Tools and Technologies Used

Coding Languages & Frameworks:

  • HTML5 Canvas, CSS3 & Modern JavaScript (ES6+) — for building the responsive UI, state-driven navigation, and high-performance 60fps rendering engine.
  • Web Audio API — for procedural synthesis of dynamic rocket ignitions, thrusters, and alert sound effects without external asset dependencies.

Software, Cloud & Prototyping Tools:

  • Vercel — for fast web deployment and live cloud hosting.
  • Canva & Google AI Studio — for UI/UX wireframing, asset design, and workflow prototyping.

    Use of Artificial Intelligence
  • Google AI Studio & Gemini — utilized for rapid logic prototyping, drafting system architecture, refining simulation physics code structures, and shaping technical documentation.

Hardware Target Architecture:

  • Browser-Native / Zero-Dependency — designed to run locally on any modern laptop, tablet, or desktop browser with no special hardware requirements.
